transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well… ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I find myself crying over things like the potluck lists, and I get all worked up about phone calls I used to handle without any problem. I’ve even started missing church planning things, and that’s not like me at all.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events?
I’m not really sure I’d say I’ve lost interest. I still care about choir and church things… I just haven’t felt quite up to being there the same way.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things in your daily life, even when there isn’t a clear reason for concern?
I’m not sure. I don’t think it’s worry all the time for no reason… it’s more that certain things feel harder to face lately. But I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about everything day to day.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or worried about everyday things more often than usual, even when there’s no clear reason?
Not really, no. I mean, I do get worked up sometimes, but I can usually point to what set it off. I haven’t noticed myself worrying about everyday things for no reason.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?

Since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. I wouldn’t say I’m sad every single minute, but I do cry over little things now, like the potluck lists, and I get worked up over calls I used to handle fine. I’ve even been missing church planning things I normally never would’ve missed.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, don't give you the same pleasure they used to since your friend passed away?

I don’t know that I’d say they don’t give me pleasure anymore. I’ve just been less steady about showing up, I guess. When I am there, parts of it can still feel good, but it’s been harder for me to get myself there like I used to.
Would you say that you’re getting less pleasure out of things you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, compared to before your friend passed away?

I’m not really sure it’s less pleasure, exactly. I still care about those things, and when I’m there I can enjoy parts of them. It’s more that I haven’t been getting myself there as easily as I used to.
Have you noticed that you have less energy than usual or feel more fatigued, even when you haven't been doing anything physically demanding?
I can’t really say I’ve noticed that, no. I mean, I get tired like anybody, but I haven’t been feeling unusually worn out when I haven’t done much.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus or concentrate on tasks, like following a conversation or keeping track of what you're doing?
I haven’t really noticed a change there. I can usually follow a conversation or keep track of what I’m doing about the same as before.
Would you say that most days, you’ve been feeling down or low in your mood since your friend passed away?

Yes… most days I’d say I haven’t felt like myself since she passed. I get tearful over little things, like the potluck lists, and I get worked up about calls that used to be easy for me. I’ve even been missing church planning things I never would’ve missed before.
Would you say you’ve lost interest in things altogether, like choir or church events, even for a little while since your friend passed away?
I don’t think I’ve lost interest altogether. I still care about choir and church things… it’s just been harder to show up or feel up to doing them sometimes.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much interest in choir or church events as you used to, even if you still care about them?

Yes, I think so. I still care about choir and the church events, but since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I’ve cried over things like the potluck lists, and I get worked up about calls I used to handle easily. I’ve even missed church planning things I never would’ve missed before.
Have you been feeling down or low in your mood most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?

Yes… since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I get upset so much easier, and little things like the potluck lists can make me cry. I’ve been missing church planning things I never would’ve missed before.
Have you found that you no longer enjoy things that used to bring you pleasure, like choir or church events, even when you're actually doing them?

I’m not sure I’d say I no longer enjoy them. I haven’t really paid attention to it that way. Sometimes I’m just… not feeling like myself, so it’s hard to tell if I’m enjoying it like I used to or not.
Would you say that your mood has been low or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?

I don’t know if I’d say it’s low all day, every day. But ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I cry over things like the potluck lists, and calls I used to handle easily get me all worked up. I’ve even missed church planning things I never would’ve missed before.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, nearly every day since your friend passed away?

I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed that nearly every day. I still go along with things sometimes, but I haven’t been paying close attention to whether I’m enjoying them the same way or not.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, nearly every day since your friend passed away?
I really can’t say it’s been nearly every day. I’ve just noticed I’m off, but I haven’t been keeping track of whether I’m enjoying choir or church things the same way each time.
Would you say that your mood has been down or depressed most of the time since your friend passed away?

Not depressed most of the time, exactly… but since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I cry over little things like the potluck lists, and calls I used to handle easy get me all worked up. I’ve even started missing church planning things I never would’ve missed before.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, more days than not since your friend passed away?

I don’t know if I’d say more days than not. I know I’ve felt different, and sometimes I’m not as into things as I used to be, but I haven’t really been counting the days or paying that close attention.
